title: Silent March Dispersal Incident, Kreuzberg
premise: Students in Berlin inadvertently spark a violent dispersal when their silent march in solidarity with climate activists is interrupted by a counter-protest carrying weapons.

side_A.role: a researcher at a human-rights NGO
side_A.goal: documenting possible excessive force by police against protesters

side_B.goal: preparing criminal charges against protesters for rioting and property damage

documents:
=== DOCUMENT 1: Incident Log – Police Unit 7, Berlin Kreuzberg ===

**Date:** 14 October 2023
**Time:** 13:30 – 14:20
**Location:** Oranienplatz / Skalitzer Straße / Weserstraße
**Officer in Charge:** Sgt. H. Weber, Unit 7
**Unit Status:** Active Deployment

**13:30** – Unit 7 deployment complete. 45 officers positioned at the perimeter of Oranienplatz. The main march route has been secured. A cordon is established at the Oranienplatz entrance, extending 50 meters deep to secure the perimeter. All officers are equipped with riot helmets and batons per protocol for potential crowd control.

**13:40** – Main march route confirmed clear. No obstructions or unauthorized gatherings within the secured zone. The silent march is scheduled to begin at 14:00.

**13:45** – Counter-protest group observed arriving at the intersection of Skalitzer Straße and Weserstraße. Visual count estimates approximately 25 individuals. The group is positioned 15 meters from the initial police line. Officers note that the counter-protesters are carrying wooden sticks; visual inspection later confirms 12 sticks in total, measuring between 60 and 80 cm in length. Body camera unit BC-71 activates recording.

**13:50** – Verbal warning issued by lead officer to disperse. The warning is broadcast via loudspeaker. The counter-protest group does not immediately retreat.

**13:52** – First physical contact reported between the groups. The situation escalates. Officers maintain position within the cordon.

**13:55 – 14:15** – Tensions remain high. The silent marchers are observed remaining largely stationary. At 14:15, three individuals identified as students from the Free University of Berlin are detained for further questioning regarding their position relative to the cordon.

**14:20** – Counter-protesters begin to retreat from the intersection. The immediate threat is neutralized. Unit 7 stands down from active dispersal mode. Incident concludes.

**14:25** – Detained students transported to temporary holding facility for processing.

**15:22** – Note: External digital evidence referenced in subsequent NGO filings.

**16:00 (15 Oct)** – Three detained students released without charge.

=== DOCUMENT 2: Witness Statement – Dr. Elena Voss ===

**Submitted by:** Dr. Elena Voss, Human Rights Researcher
**Date of Statement:** 18 October 2023
**Context:** Observation of the Silent March Dispersal Incident, Kreuzberg

I was present at the Oranienplatz on 14 October 2023 to monitor the compliance of the silent march with local regulations. The atmosphere was tense, but the marchers were disciplined. As per the agreed protocol, the silent marchers did not make any vocal shouts or use megaphones during the initial 30 minutes. This was crucial to maintaining the peaceful nature of the assembly.

The counter-protest group, which I counted at approximately 25 individuals, arrived at the intersection of Skalitzer Straße and Weserstraße at 13:45. They were clearly agitated and carried wooden sticks. It is undeniable that they initiated the physical confrontation by advancing on the silent marchers first. They moved aggressively toward the cordon, ignoring the distance that had been maintained.

At 13:50, a verbal warning was issued. However, before the police could establish a legitimate threat assessment, the officers charged into the group. I believe police used disproportionate force by charging into the group before any threat was established. The officers, wearing riot helmets and holding batons, acted with excessive aggression given that the counter-protesters had not yet made full contact with the marchers.

The dispersal order was unlawful because the silent march had not violated any specific regulation at that moment. The marchers were silent and orderly. The police created a crisis by reacting to the presence of the counter-protesters rather than enforcing the law.

Regarding the students, I was in close proximity to the three Free University students who were arrested at 14:15. The students remained passive and did not engage in any provocative behavior. They were standing still, observing the situation, and did not attempt to cross any lines. Their arrest was arbitrary. The video file 'ORAN_1348.mp4', which was uploaded to our server at 15:22 that same day, captures this moment clearly. It shows the police pushing the students away while they remained non-compliant but passive. The incident ended at 14:20 when the counter-protesters retreated, but the damage to the rule of law was already done.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement – Klaus Braun ===

**Submitted by:** Klaus Braun, Public Prosecutor
**Date of Statement:** 18 October 2023
**Context:** Legal Assessment of the Silent March Dispersal Incident, Kreuzberg

I reviewed the body camera footage from unit BC-71, which recorded the scene from 13:45 to 14:20 on 14 October 2023. The footage corroborates the police report regarding the deployment of Unit 7. By 13:30, 45 officers were deployed, and the cordon was 50 meters deep at the Oranienplatz entrance. The main march route was cleared by 13:40.

The critical issue is the conduct of the silent marchers. Contrary to the claims of the NGO, the silent marchers broke the police cordon and advanced toward the counter-protesters, initiating the confrontation. At 13:45, the counter-protest group was at the intersection of Skalitzer Straße and Weserstraße, 15 meters from the police line. They were carrying 12 wooden sticks, measured between 60 and 80 cm in length. Police records indicate that this counter-protest group had previously been involved in 3 violent incidents in 2022. This history is relevant to the assessment of risk.

When the silent marchers began to push against the cordon, the police issued a verbal warning to disperse at 13:50. The first physical contact occurred at 13:52. Police force was proportionate and necessary to prevent imminent violence from the armed counter-protesters. The officers were equipped with riot helmets and batons, which is standard for such deployments. The charge was a tactical response to the breach of the cordon by the marchers, not an unprovoked aggression.

The dispersal order was lawful because the presence of armed counter-protesters created an immediate public safety risk. The combination of the marchers breaking the cordon and the armed nature of the counter-protesters necessitated immediate intervention.

Regarding the students, the footage shows that the students actively provoked the counter-protesters by moving closer to them despite police warnings. They were not passive. They were positioned in a way that escalated the tension, leading to their detention at 14:15. Their release without charge at 16:00 on 15 October 2023 was a result of the lack of sufficient evidence for a criminal charge, not an admission of police error. The incident ended at 14:20 when the counter-protesters retreated, but the police action was justified up to that point.

=== DOCUMENT 4: Email – Legal Team Review ===

**From:** Legal Team, Berlin NGO for Civil Rights
**To:** Dr. Elena Voss
**Date:** 17 October 2023
**Subject:** Review of Body Camera Footage – Kreuzberg Incident

Dr. Voss,

We have completed our preliminary review of the video evidence provided by the police. The police body camera unit BC-71 recorded the scene from 13:45 to 14:20 on 14 October 2023. Our legal team reviewed 4 hours of continuous body camera footage from various angles to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the sequence of events.

We have noted the following key timestamps from the footage:
- 13:45: Counter-protest group arrives at the intersection.
- 13:50: Verbal warning issued.
- 13:52: First physical contact.
- 14:15: Arrest of three students.
- 14:20: Incident ends.

The footage confirms that the counter-protesters were carrying wooden sticks. Our count aligns with the police report of 12 sticks, measuring between 60 and 80 cm. We also note that the silent marchers remained silent for the initial 30 minutes, as per the march protocol.

We have filed a formal complaint with the Berlin Interior Ministry on 16 October 2023. The complaint focuses on the proportionality of the police response and the legality of the dispersal order. We argue that the police action was disproportionate given that the silent marchers had not violated any specific regulation prior to the police charge.

We are currently preparing a detailed timeline for submission to the Interior Ministry. We will also be providing the video file 'ORAN_1348.mp4', which was uploaded to our server at 15:22 on 14 October 2023, as supplementary evidence. This file captures the moment of the students' arrest and the subsequent retreat of the counter-protesters.

Please review the attached timeline and let us know if you have any additional observations to add to the formal complaint.

Regards,
Legal Team

=== DOCUMENT 5: Medical and Incident Inspection Report ===

**Report ID:** MED-2023-1014-003
**Date of Inspection:** 14 October 2023
**Location:** Kreuzberg Police Holding Facility
**Inspected By:** Dr. A. Schmidt, Medical Examiner
**Subject:** Physical Condition of Detained Individuals

**Inspection Time:** 15:30 – 15:45
**Individuals Inspected:** 3 (Students from Free University of Berlin)

**Findings:**
1.  **Individual 1:** Minor abrasions on left forearm. No signs of significant trauma. States no injury prior to detention.
2.  **Individual 2:** Bruising on right shoulder. States no injury prior to detention.
3.  **Individual 3:** No visible injuries.

**Context:**
The individuals were detained at 14:15 on 14 October 2023. The detention was related to the Silent March Dispersal Incident. The police cordon was 50 meters deep at the Oranienplatz entrance. The main march route was cleared by 13:40. The counter-protest group, estimated at 25 individuals, arrived at 13:45 at the intersection of Skalitzer Straße and Weserstraße. The distance between the initial police line and the counter-protest group was 15 meters at 13:45.

The police issued a verbal warning to disperse at 13:50. The first physical contact between groups occurred at 13:52. The incident ended at 14:20 when the counter-protesters retreated. The students were released without charge at 16:00 on 15 October 2023.

The medical examination does not indicate any injuries consistent with excessive force. The minor abrasions and bruising are consistent with accidental contact during crowd dispersal. The police officers were wearing riot helmets and holding batons during the dispersal phase. The counter-protesters were carrying 12 wooden sticks, measured between 60 and 80 cm in length.

The report is submitted for the record. No further medical action is required.

**Signature:**
Dr. A. Schmidt
Medical Examiner
